nodes.description: Owned.owner: privileged owner address initialized in constructor and updated by acceptOwnership
Owned.newOwner: pending owner address set by transferOwnership and consumed by acceptOwnership
BXB.symbol token ticker string set in constructor
BXB.name token name string set in constructor
BXB.decimals token precision set in constructor
BXB._totalSupply total token supply returned by totalSupply()
BXB.balances mapping(address=>uint) holding account token balances
BXB.allowed nested mapping of owner=>spender=>amount allowances
SafeMath.safeAdd(uint a, uint b): addition with require(c >= a) overflow check
SafeMath.safeSub(uint a, uint b): subtraction with require(b <= a) underflow check
SafeMath.safeMul(uint a, uint b): multiplication with division consistency check
SafeMath.safeDiv(uint a, uint b): division with require(b > 0) zero-division check
Owned constructor assigning the hard-coded owner address
Owned.transferOwnership(address _newOwner) onlyOwner: stages new owner
Owned.acceptOwnership(): caller must equal newOwner, finalizes ownership transfer
BXB constructor: sets metadata, _totalSupply and pre-mints entire supply to owner
BXB.totalSupply() view returning _totalSupply
BXB.balanceOf(address tokenOwner) view returning balances[tokenOwner]
BXB.transfer(address to, uint tokens): moves tokens from msg.sender to recipient
BXB.approve(address spender, uint tokens): writes allowance for msg.sender
BXB.transferFrom(address from, address to, uint tokens): spends allowance and moves tokens
BXB.allowance(address tokenOwner, address spender) view returning remaining allowance
BXB.approveAndCall(address spender, uint tokens, bytes data): approves then calls receiveApproval on spender
BXB.receive() external payable that unconditionally reverts incoming ETH
BXB.transferAnyERC20Token(address tokenAddress, uint tokens) onlyOwner: rescues arbitrary ERC20 tokens
msg.sender evaluated in the onlyOwner modifier: require(msg.sender == owner)
msg.sender used as the acting account in transfer/approve/transferFrom/approveAndCall
msg.sender evaluated in acceptOwnership: require(msg.sender == newOwner)
Arithmetic in safeAdd: c = a + b (uint overflow boundary checked by require(c >= a))
Arithmetic in safeSub: c = a - b (uint underflow boundary checked by require(b <= a))
Arithmetic in safeMul: c = a * b with require(a == 0 || c / a == b)
Arithmetic in safeDiv: c = a / b with require(b > 0)
External call ApproveAndCallFallBack(spender).receiveApproval(msg.sender, tokens, address(this), data) to an attacker-controlled address before state settles
External call IERC20(tokenAddress).transfer(owner, tokens) on an arbitrary caller-supplied token contract
_newOwner parameter of transferOwnership
to parameter of transfer
tokens parameter of transfer
spender parameter of approve
tokens parameter of approve
from parameter of transferFrom
to parameter of transferFrom
tokens parameter of transferFrom
spender parameter of approveAndCall, also the external call target
tokens parameter of approveAndCall
data parameter of approveAndCall, forwarded to receiveApproval
tokenAddress parameter of transferAnyERC20Token, also the external call target
tokens parameter of transferAnyERC20Token
tokenOwner parameter of balanceOf, used as balance mapping key

edges.reason: Owned constructor writes the privileged owner state variable, establishing the authorization root
BXB constructor assigns the fixed _totalSupply value
BXB constructor pre-mints the entire supply into balances[owner]
transferOwnership writes the untrusted _newOwner value into the newOwner state variable
onlyOwner modifier gates transferOwnership on msg.sender == owner
acceptOwnership gates execution on msg.sender == newOwner, an attacker-reachable ownership path if newOwner is set
acceptOwnership overwrites the owner state variable and clears newOwner
transfer uses msg.sender as the key into the balances mapping for debit and credit
transfer reads and writes the balances state mapping
transfer debits balances[msg.sender] through safeSub, where underflow is only implied by the require check
transfer credits balances[to] through safeAdd, where overflow is only implied by the require check
to parameter supplies the recipient key for the balances credit in transfer
tokens parameter supplies the directly user-controlled amount moved in transfer
approve writes the allowed allowance mapping without a zeroing step (double-spend approval race)
approve uses msg.sender as the owner key of the allowed mapping
spender parameter becomes the second key of the allowed allowance mapping
tokens parameter becomes the approved allowance amount
transferFrom reads and writes balances for the from and to accounts
transferFrom decreases allowed[from][msg.sender] before the external observers see the transfer
transferFrom uses safeSub on both the source balance and the spender allowance
transferFrom uses safeAdd to credit the destination balance
transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spender key in the allowed mapping
from parameter supplies the account debited by transferFrom
to parameter supplies the account credited by transferFrom
tokens parameter supplies the amount debited from balance and allowance
approveAndCall writes the allowed allowance mapping for msg.sender and spender
approveAndCall passes msg.sender as the from argument of receiveApproval
approveAndCall performs an external callback into the spender contract via receiveApproval after mutating allowance state
spender parameter is cast to ApproveAndCallFallBack, letting the caller choose the external call target
tokens parameter is written into allowed and forwarded to receiveApproval
data parameter is forwarded verbatim to the external receiveApproval call
The external callee can re-enter approveAndCall while the allowance write is not yet reconciled with the token accounting
The external callee can re-enter transfer and move balances while the approveAndCall flow is in progress
transferAnyERC20Token executes transfer on a caller-supplied ERC20 contract, an external callback
onlyOwner modifier gates transferAnyERC20Token on msg.sender == owner
tokenAddress parameter selects the arbitrary external contract invoked by the owner-only rescue function
tokens parameter is forwarded as the amount to the external ERC20 transfer
balanceOf reads the balances state mapping
tokenOwner parameter is used directly as the balances mapping lookup key
safeAdd body contains the addition whose overflow is guarded only by require(c >= a)
safeSub body contains the subtraction whose underflow is guarded only by require(b <= a)
safeMul body contains the multiplication whose overflow is guarded by the division consistency check
safeDiv body contains the division guarded by require(b > 0)
totalSupply returns the _totalSupply state variable
allowance reads the allowed nested mapping
_newOwner parameter is assigned into the newOwner state variable by transferOwnership

normalization_plan.reason: The _newOwner parameter only carries data into transferOwnership, which writes it to the newOwner state variable
The to parameter is a pure data carrier for the balances credit inside transfer
The tokens parameter is consumed only by the safeSub/safeAdd arithmetic inside transfer
The spender parameter is only used as the allowed mapping key inside approve
The tokens parameter is only stored into the allowed allowance inside approve
The from parameter only selects the balances/allowed keys inside transferFrom
The to parameter only selects the balances credit key inside transferFrom
The tokens parameter is consumed by the safeSub/safeAdd accounting inside transferFrom
The spender parameter becomes the target of the external receiveApproval call, the reentrancy-relevant unsafe operation
The tokens parameter flows only into the allowance write and the forwarded call arguments inside approveAndCall
The data parameter is passed straight through approveAndCall into the external call payload
The tokenAddress parameter determines the external contract invoked by the low-trust external transfer call
The tokens parameter is only forwarded as the transfer amount inside transferAnyERC20Token
The tokenOwner parameter is only used as the balances lookup key inside balanceOf
